newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain court declassifies secret "dirty war" papers.
newsitem.headline: Spain court declassifies secret "dirty war" papers.

text.p: Spain's Supreme Court ordered the declassification on Saturday of secret spy papers purporting to show the former Socialist government of Felipe Gonzalez ran death squads in a 1980s "dirty war" against ETA rebels.

The ruling, announced in a court communique, overturns a decision last year by the new Conservative government to keep the so-called CESID papers secret for reasons of state security. The documents could provide evidence leading to the reopening of investigations of Gonzalez and other senior officials in his administration.

After four days of deliberations, the 33 magistrates decided the government must open 13 of 18 classified documents sought by three lower courts to prove Gonzalez's government masterminded "anti-terrorist" squads to fight the violent separatist group ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).
Twenty-eight people were killed from 1983-1987 in the squads' campaign of kidnappings and torture. ETA has killed some 800 people in a 29-year drive for Basque independence from Spain.

Though Supreme Court justices probing the death squads have decided against questioning Gonzalez to date, the scandal tainted the Socialists and contributed to their election defeat in March 1996 after 13 years in power.
Judges and Spain's Attorney General Juan Ortiz Urculo have said investigations of Gonzalez and his associates could be reopened if new evidence emerges from the CESID documents.
